title: U.S. Senate · Illinois

context.text: The seat is open. Incumbent Sen. Dick Durbin (D), first elected in 1996, announced on April 23, 2025 that he would not seek re-election.

Lt. Gov. Juliana Stratton won the March 17, 2026 Democratic primary over U.S. Reps. Robin Kelly and Raja Krishnamoorthi and several other candidates. Don Tracy, former chair of the Illinois Republican Party, won the Republican primary.

summary.text: Juliana Stratton is the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate and the sitting Lieutenant Governor of Illinois. A Chicago attorney and mediator who worked on criminal justice policy in Cook County, she served one term in the Illinois House before being elected lieutenant governor alongside J.B. Pritzker in 2018. She won the March 17, 2026 Democratic primary with 40.4% of the vote.

background.text: Born in Chicago on September 8, 1965, and raised in the Pill Hill neighborhood on the city's South Side. She attended Kenwood Academy.
Earned a bachelor's degree in broadcast journalism from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign in 1987 and a J.D. from DePaul University College of Law in 1992.

Worked as a video producer for the city of Chicago, then as an attorney; in 1997 she founded JDS Mediation Services and served as an arbitrator and administrative law judge for several City of Chicago agencies.

Taught conflict management and negotiation at Loyola University Chicago, and was executive director of the Cook County Justice Advisory Council (2011-2014) and director of the Center for Public Safety and Justice at the University of Illinois at Chicago (2015-2017).
Won the 2016 Democratic primary for the Illinois House's 5th District, defeating incumbent Ken Dunkin with 68% of the vote, and served in the House from 2017 to 2019.
Was announced in August 2017 as J.B. Pritzker's running mate and was elected Lieutenant Governor in November 2018, taking office in January 2019. She and Pritzker were re-elected in 2022.

As lieutenant governor, she launched the Justice, Equity, and Opportunity Initiative and chairs the Illinois Council on Women and Girls and several other state councils, according to Wikipedia's account.

Announced her U.S. Senate campaign in April 2025 after Sen. Dick Durbin said he would not seek re-election, and won the Democratic primary over U.S. Reps. Raja Krishnamoorthi and Robin Kelly and others.

priorities.text: "To me, Illinois is the blueprint. What Governor Pritzker and I have done here in Illinois is the blueprint that I want to take to Washington, D.C., and I want to fight for Illinoisans just like I've done for seven years."
Released an economic plan that she said "includes pathways to lowering the cost of housing, healthcare, and everyday prices while building an economy for working people."

"What I'm just seeing is that the old playbook in Washington, D.C., isn't working. People aren't... looking for people to just talk. They want to see real action, and that's exactly what we've done in our administration."

positions.summary: Said she supports Medicare for All.

candidates.name: Don Tracy
candidates.currentRole: Attorney, Brown, Hay & Stephens; former chair of the Illinois Republican Party

summary.text: Don Tracy is the Republican nominee for U.S. Senate in Illinois. A Springfield attorney, he chaired the Illinois Gaming Board from 2015 to 2019 and the Illinois Republican Party beginning in 2021. He says he is running to represent all 102 Illinois counties and focuses on the cost of living.

background.text: Born in Urbana, Illinois; says he was raised in Mt. Sterling and raised his own family in Springfield.
Earned a bachelor's degree from Arizona State University and a law degree from the University of Memphis.
Says he began working in his family's business at age 10 and later ran a small business.
Is an attorney at the Springfield law firm Brown, Hay & Stephens, where WGLT reported in 2021 that he was a partner.

Chaired the Illinois Gaming Board from February 2015 until June 2019, during Gov. Bruce Rauner's administration. He resigned after the state Office of Executive Inspector General reported that he had engaged in improper political activity by making several campaign contributions while serving on the board, in violation of the Riverboat Gambling Act.
Was named chairman of the Illinois Republican Party in February 2021, succeeding Tim Schneider; he was the first party chairman since 1988 not from Chicago or the collar counties.
Says he has served on boards including the Abraham Lincoln Association and the Sangamon County Bar.

priorities.text: "I'm Don Tracy, and I'm running for U.S. Senate because the American Dream is slipping away for too many working families here in our state... My top priority: lower costs so families can thrive again."
Says he will be a voice for all 102 Illinois counties, not just Chicago.
Says he wants to find solutions to lower the cost of living, citing utility, housing, gas, grocery, and health-care costs.

positions.summary: Says Illinois suffers under "the highest tax burden in the nation" and criticizes what he calls "tax-and-spend policies," opposing further tax increases.
positions.quote: With the cost-of-living continuing to rise, life is simply unaffordable for working families — especially in Illinois, where we suffer under the highest tax burden in the nation and endure an economy that lags the rest of the Midwest because of tax-and-spend Democrats.

candidates.name: Whitfield Harrington Jr.
candidates.currentRole: Pastor, Prayer City of Chicago Church

summary.text: Whitfield Harrington Jr. is the American Center Party candidate for U.S. Senate in Illinois. He is a pastor in Chicago who previously worked in banking, insurance and financial services. He describes his campaign as an independent, centrist alternative focused on affordability and opportunity.

background.text: Born in Belzoni, Mississippi, the twentieth of 21 children, by his own account.
Earned a bachelor's degree in political science from Delta State University in 2002.
Worked in banking, insurance and financial services, including operating his own insurance practice.
Moved to Chicago in 2013 and serves as pastor of Prayer City of Chicago Church; says he lives in Schaumburg, Illinois.

priorities.text: "Renovate the American Dream" platform addresses cost of living through job creation, manufacturing, affordable homeownership pathways, lower health-care costs, and tax changes.

Running as an independent "Move to the Middle" candidate, saying he wants to focus on "practical problem-solving, congressional and government reform, and consideration of policies based on their results rather than their party origin."
Platform proposals include expanding Direct Primary Care, making the first year of community college free, supporting domestic manufacturing, and protecting farmers' right to repair equipment.
